text: Terrible experience. My first visit was for teeth whitening, but it included a scaling procedure. The male dentist was very rough and seemed rushed, and he wasn't careful. It felt like the scaling instrument almost scratched my teeth; it was painful. The instrument should have been on my teeth, but it was right where I had a wound. When I rinsed, I was shocked because the water was darker red with blood than anywhere else I've had scaling done. The dentist didn't say anything. When I got home, I was sure I had a wound, so I checked and confirmed it was. The assistant seemed to be on their phone and not paying attention to the patient because the light illuminating my teeth went out for a while, but they didn't do anything. I only heard a video clip (it was my first time, so I didn't know that the light going out meant the procedure was complete, as the assistant didn't do anything else, so I thought I had to wait). I'm very disappointed. The clinic looked better than the surrounding areas, and I came because of an event, but this experience was very unpleasant. However, the counter staff were nice and cheerful. Please improve this.

text:
I am extremely disappointed with this consultation.

I went in with the intention of inquiring about information and seeking a medical opinion regarding permanent wire retainers, as I have concerns about wearing removable retainers long-term. However, what I received was not impartial information or a genuine listening experience.

During the conversation, it was clear the doctor had a judgmental attitude towards my opinions and spoke in a way that made me feel uninformed, blindly following trends rather than genuinely trying to understand my concerns.

Strangely, at one point, they suggested I consult my current orthodontist, but later said that I would get the same answer anywhere. This is despite my own orthodontist stating that it was possible. It felt like the doctor was more focused on blocking differing opinions than explaining the pros and cons to help me make my own decision.

Not getting a permanent wire retainer isn't the issue, as it's ultimately the doctor's prerogative to accept or reject the case. However, making me feel uninformed, that my questions were worthless, and that I was being lectured rather than receiving proper advice is unacceptable.

I will not be using their services again and would not recommend them to anyone seeking consultation from a doctor who is open to diverse opinions and genuinely listens to their needs.
